# loanflow integer-input convention (LFCONV-INTGUARD-01)

Design note for the loanflow demo package.

Any loanflow value that is semantically an integer (cents, basis points, credit
scores, day counts) is guarded with the same two-part check, in this order:

    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
        raise ValidationError("<name> must be an integer ...")

Why the `bool` test comes first: `bool` is a subclass of `int` in Python, so
`isinstance(True, int)` is `True` and a plain `isinstance(value, int)` check
silently accepts `True`/`False`. Floats such as `10.5` must also be rejected
rather than compared against thresholds.

Where it already lives: `Money.__post_init__` and `Percentage.__post_init__` in
`loanflow/primitives.py`, and `classify_credit_score` in `loanflow/risk_bands.py`.
The error type is always `loanflow.errors.ValidationError`, and the type check runs
before any range/threshold check. Each guard gets a `pytest.raises(ValidationError)`
regression test in the module's own `tests/unit/test_<module>.py`.
